Contact: (704) 560-9101 · ingibjorg.draper@exprealty.com

## About

Inga Draper is a REALTOR® with eXp Realty based in the Charlotte, North Carolina metro
area. Her practice covers residential purchases and sales, out-of-state relocation, and
property strategy for owners deciding whether to sell, hold, or rent. She is licensed in
both North Carolina and South Carolina and publishes local market commentary on YouTube
as "Inga in the QC".

## Answers

Each page below answers one specific question directly.

- [What should I know before relocating to Charlotte?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/relocating-to-charlotte/): Choose commute tolerance before neighborhood; verify school assignment at the parcel level.
- [What does a first-time buyer need to know in Charlotte?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/first-time-home-buyer-charlotte/): North Carolina's due diligence fee is generally non-refundable and must be budgeted as money at risk.
- [What should I check before buying an investment property near Lake Norman?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/buying-investment-property-lake-norman/): Verify local rules, recorded restrictions, insurance, flood information, utilities, and Duke Energy shoreline records before modeling income.
- [How does the due diligence fee work in North Carolina?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/north-carolina-due-diligence-fee/): The fee is negotiated, usually credited at closing, and generally lost if the buyer cancels.
- [How do I verify the school assignment for a Charlotte-area address?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/verify-school-assignment-charlotte-lake-norman/): Use the governing district's official lookup for the full address and correct school year.
- [What should I verify before buying Lake Norman waterfront property?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/lake-norman-waterfront-property-checks/): Check dock and shoreline approvals, flood information, utilities, and private restrictions for the exact property.
- [How do I verify zoning before buying in the Charlotte area?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/verify-zoning-before-buying-charlotte-area/): Ask the responsible city, town, or county about the exact address and intended use.
